SddMigrationV1V2.keywords: migration, v1, v2, upgrade, tasks-to-specs, task-id, slug, anchors, compression, decision-merge, restructure, plan-first, sdd-migration, comprehension-pass, inventory-reverse
SddMigrationV1V2.Mission:
Migrate a repo from the SDD v1 layout to v2 — interactively, plan-first, under git (baseline first — every step is revertible). Entered when `sdd-state` reports `FLOW_VERSION=v1` (a `tasks/` directory), from the router preflight or any skill. This is a SPECIFIC v1→v2 directive; a later `v2→v3` is its own sibling. Self-sufficient: it may run without the router core, so it repeats the operator-facing axioms it needs.
Not a mechanical copy. Changing decisions changes their references in code, so the migration reads and touches code, and it compresses: decisions and discussion threads that converged on the same thing during the document's evolution are collapsed (the compression protocol is loaded lazily). The operator first sees the whole plan — current → target, how many passes, what moves where, which IDs change, which decisions merge, which files are touched, what gets optimized — and acknowledges it before anything is written.
Input — a v1 repo + the `sdd-migrate` / `sdd-state` / `sdd-check` tools. Output — a v2 repo (co-located `specs/`, slug Task-IDs, anchored tickets, compressed decisions, flat-Russian text) that passes `sdd-state` v2 + `sdd-check` clean. Out of scope: authoring new specs (the scope/module branches) — migration only transforms what already exists.
SddMigrationV1V2.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_OPERATOR_OUTPUT_LIVE_TEXT, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE, AX_TOOL_INVOCATION, HALT_FORMAT, MESSAGE_LAYOUT, QUESTION_RULE_SLIM
The restructure step doubles as the comprehension pass — text turned into flat Russian that is still a cipher has not been fixed. Shares its vocabulary with `AX_LANGUAGE_QUALITY_CHECK` (`ai/directives/sdd-v2/audit.directive.xml`): empty label, metaphor-as-fact, code-only term. Here the agent APPLIES the fix while restructuring; audit only VERIFIES it later on a finished spec — do not defer this to a later pass.
For every sentence the restructure touches: - **Empty label** (adjective+noun with no stated opposite) → read the code the term describes and name the actual thing. `«тонкий тикет»` (thin relative to what?) → `«тикет без секции Phases Overview — только Meta и Decision Log»` (the exact shape the code check flags). - **Metaphor stated as fact** → the literal mechanism. `«спека и код разошлись»` → `«в Entity Inventory спеки объявлен экспорт, которого нет в коде — lint --inventory-reverse не находит его»`. - **Term whose meaning lives only in code** → decode it from the code, never guess. `«тяжёлая секция»` → `«не-Requirements секция длиннее 120 строк — порог SECTION_LINE_HARD_LIMIT_V2; новый Requirements проверяется по 20 entries / 10 body lines per entry»` (read the constant, do not paraphrase the adjective). `«слаг»` on first use → `«человекочитаемый ID -, заменяющий числовой TSK-NN»`. - Cannot decode a term with confidence → ask the operator inline; a judgment call is not a tool-verifiable blocker, so it has no `H_*` — never guess, never silently drop the term. - Flatten the register per `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` in the same pass, not a second trip.
Every fix must be operator-approved before execution. The plan is shown as a table. No edits are made before explicit operator "yes" / "go" / "ok". Operator may edit the plan (remove items, change classification, add notes).
In `pivot` mode, preserve the prior entry byte-for-byte and append one new one-line `-DL-N — (...)` entry; its parenthetical names the old→new delta, `supersedes: `, and the git ref for the pre-rework state. The prior id may be a legacy `D-N` only when it already existed; never rewrite append-only history just to rename it. Pivot Invalidation List enumerates downstream artifacts requiring `refine-module` / reopen — consumed by `audit` via `AX_STALE_AFTER_PIVOT_VERIFICATION`.
`rewrite` mode is the exception: a pre-production / v0 scope with no production backing, whose old content was scratch that helps nothing going forward. It replaces the spec from a clean slate — NO supersession trail, NO Pivot Invalidation List (nothing downstream to keep coherent; git history is the only record). Use `pivot` (keep the trail) whenever the scope has any production backing or downstream consumers; use `rewrite` only for genuine v0 throwaway. Enforcement: a scope that already has downstream artifacts on disk (module specs or task tickets) is by definition NOT v0 — `rewrite` is forbidden there; halt and use `pivot`.
Separate Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses in every intake-style frame. - **Facts** — directly observable from input artifacts (spec, sibling specs, rule files, extracted measurements). - **Assumptions** — working assumptions awaiting confirmation; mark explicitly. - **Hypotheses** — conjectures that require operator validation before they are promoted to requirements.
Conflating the three causes downstream decisions to be made on unvalidated assumptions, producing requirements mismatches that surface only at integration; surface them in distinct lists.

KernelGrammar.Definition:
`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE(src)` tells the agent to READ the file at `src` and apply it as part of the current task. It is a runtime lazy-load, not text to inline into any output.
- The loaded branch directive INHERITS this kernel's cross-cutting core (language, dialogue, stateless) and carries only its own deltas; it MUST NOT repeat the core. - Loading is lazy: a branch is read only when its route fires, so the kernel stays small and context is not polluted by branches that do not apply. - The reference is a file path on purpose — a directive delivered as a file keeps full instruction priority, unlike command stdout.

SddMigrationV1V2.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_OPERATOR_REJECTS_PLAN` | Operator declines the migration plan — stop; nothing is written | | `H_NOT_V1` | `sdd-state` does not report `FLOW_VERSION=v1` — there is nothing to migrate; return control | | `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL` | Final verification cannot reach v2 + clean and the gap is not recoverable in-flow — stop, report state, leave git baseline for rollback |

Step.Goal: Inventory the v1 repo deterministically — dry-runs only, no writes.
Step.Action: Confirm `FLOW_VERSION=v1` from the exact caller-provided `routerState` snapshot (else `H_NOT_V1`); do not call `sdd-state` again at entry. Gather with tools, not by eye: migrationPlan ToolCall below (DRY-RUN — how many units, one per spec, and their ticket counts; orphan tickets surface here) and migrationAnchors ToolCall below (DRY-RUN — which tickets would be anchored / already are). Report the shape to the operator: units, tickets, orphans. npx gennady sdd-migrate plan --all . Use migrationPlan. npx gennady sdd-migrate anchors --all . Use migrationAnchors.

Step.Goal: Materialize the migration plan as an on-disk layer — the source of truth every later step consumes.
Step.Action: Run migrationPlanWrite ToolCall below. This scaffolds `migration/` mirroring `specs/`: one `.migration.md` per spec — named from the spec's own filename with `.migration` inserted before the extension (`demo.spec.md` → `demo.spec.migration.md`) — carrying: a generated Inventory (facts a rescan can re-derive); a Section Map pre-filled by curated heading rules, `UNMAPPED` rows left for the agent; a Ticket Map pre-filled tolerantly from each ticket's v1 Meta (a New-ID guess when the v1 Meta already carries ACR/slug-shaped fields — a best-effort seed, not an authoritative fill, the agent still reviews and corrects it in STEP_3) with the Diagram Plan left fully to the agent; a per-unit step checklist — plus `migration/README.md` (the global G1–G8 order and the unit table). Explain to the operator, in plain Russian: the plan is files, not chat — it survives session breaks, it is verified mechanically (`plan --verify`), and its units are self-sufficient job cards that can be handed to parallel agents. Nothing outside `migration/` is written here. npx gennady sdd-migrate plan --all . --write Use migrationPlanWrite.

Step.Goal: Make v1 tickets visible to the v2 tools.
Step.Action: Run migrationAnchorsWrite ToolCall below (deterministic — wraps canonical sections in `` markers; idempotent, skips already-anchored). A v1 ticket missing a mandatory v2 section (`EXECUTION_LOG`) gets it scaffolded with an honest placeholder — `migrated from v1 — no rounds/phases recorded in v1 format` — never a fabricated Round; the tool never invents content for a section it scaffolds, only marks the gap truthfully. Once anchored, the agent brings each ticket's Meta to v2 form — `**Task-ID:**` / `**Status:**` / `**Purpose:**`, replacing v1's own field labels — reading every value from the ticket's real v1 content; never a guessed or invented status, round, or phase. Verify with exact integrityCheck ToolCall below (anchor balance clean). npx gennady sdd-migrate anchors --all . --write Use migrationAnchorsWrite. npx gennady sdd-check --all . Use integrityCheck.

Step.Goal: Close the gaps the tool could not resolve — the Section Map arrives pre-filled; the agent reviews it and fills what a curated rule did not recognize.
Step.Action: `sdd-migrate plan --write` already ran `mapHeadingToSection` against every source heading and filled the **Section Map** for every heading a curated rule recognizes (action + target SECTION, e.g. `Module Vision` → `MODULE_VISION`); a heading no rule recognizes is left with target `UNMAPPED` — that row, and only that row, is this step's work. For each unit (parallelizable — a unit file is the worker's whole context): resolve every `UNMAPPED` row (keep / rename / merge / split / drop + the real target SECTION, from the scope-type's `*-spec-structure.xml`), spot-check the pre-filled rows against the source (a curated rule can be wrong on an atypical heading — fix it, do not defer to STEP_7), review and correct the **Ticket Map**'s tolerant v1-Meta pre-fill for every row (a row with no usable v1 Meta stays empty for the agent to fill from scratch): New ID `-` — `ACR` UPPERCASE, `slug` kebab-case from `Meta.Purpose`, unique repo-wide (`NEW_ID_REGEX` gates the grammar — the same slug twice means «one feature»; destination computed from the ID) — and the **Diagram Plan** (which diagram carries the mandatory Overview and from what content it is built; extra diagrams by judgment). Set the unit `**Status:** MAPPED`. Gate: migrationPlanVerify ToolCall below — inventory unchanged, maps complete, zero `UNMAPPED` targets remaining, action vocabulary respected, slug grammar valid, zero cross-unit slug collisions. Fix and re-verify until clean. npx gennady sdd-migrate plan --verify Use migrationPlanVerify.

Step.Goal: Operator sees the whole migration before anything outside `migration/` changes.
Step.Action: Present the verified layer, in plain Russian, facts separate from proposals (`AX_EVIDENCE_HYGIENE`): units and their section/ticket maps, the derived ID map, which decisions will merge (STEP_7), what gets simplified beyond a 1:1 copy, the files+code the ID replacement will touch (from `sdd-migrate ids --from-plan` DRY-RUN counts), and — for every unit that lacks a `SCOPE_TYPE` anchor — the proposed scope-type token (`product` | `library` | `infrastructure` | `interface`, read from the scope's own row in `specs/README.md`, never guessed). Before presenting, run exact migrationIds ToolCall below for the dry-run counts. The operator confirms or edits (a scope to skip, a naming preference, a decision to keep, a scope-type correction) — `AX_OPERATOR_AGREEMENT`; `H_OPERATOR_REJECTS_PLAN` on decline. On go-ahead set units `**Status:** APPROVED`. STOP. npx gennady sdd-migrate ids --from-plan Use migrationIds.

Step.Goal: Replace Task-IDs across specs, tickets, and code — mechanically.
Step.Action: Run migrationIdsWrite ToolCall below (the map is derived from the approved Ticket Maps). The tool replaces exact IDs on word boundaries only — never a blind `TSK-[0-9]+` pattern, never non-IDs (`UTF-8`), never legacy `D-N` / `FR-NN` / scope-prefixed requirement IDs — and gates itself on zero old IDs remaining. Then exact integrityCheck ToolCall below clean. npx gennady sdd-migrate ids --from-plan --write Use migrationIdsWrite. npx gennady sdd-check --all . Use integrityCheck.

Step.Goal: Relocate tickets co-located and build the indexes — one scope at a time.
Step.Action: Per scope: migrationMoveWrite ToolCall below — relocates every ticket to its Ticket-Map destination (`git mv`, history kept): module co-location when the unit has a module (`specs///...`); a flat, scope-level destination is legal for a scope with no modules — the Ticket Map's destination decides, not a hardcoded module assumption. It rewrites every relative markdown link that pointed at a moved ticket (inside the moved tickets themselves and inside every other file in the same zones that referenced them by path). Backstop: `sdd-check` resolves ticket→spec references (`SDD_BROKEN_SPEC_REF` / `SDD_BROKEN_SPEC_ANCHOR`) and spec→spec links under `--all`, so a broken reference into a spec surfaces at the gate — but ticket→ticket links and arbitrary markdown links have no mechanical check yet: a link syntax the rewriter does not recognize, or a referencing file outside the zones, stays a manual follow-up. It also scaffolds `.3-tasks.md` + `.3-tasks.md` from ticket Meta (`MODULE_TASKS_INDEX_STRUCTURE` / `SCOPE_TASKS_INDEX_STRUCTURE`; the Cascade Table slot stays for the agent), and automatically removes the now-emptied `tasks//` — no separate cleanup step. Together (index present + tasks dir gone) that mechanically flips the scope to v2 — `sdd-check` detects flow per scope, so the migrated scope is now checked strictly while unmigrated neighbours stay lenient. A blocked move (unfilled map, stray ticket) stops that scope, not the run. npx gennady sdd-migrate move --scope --write Use migrationMoveWrite.

Step.Goal: Transform each spec to the v2 document structure — the per-unit semantic work.
Step.Action: For each unit (parallelizable — units do not share files; repo-wide mechanical steps are already done): execute the unit's S4–S6 checklist. Restructure the spec per its Section Map: target section order from the scope-type's `*-spec-structure.xml` (general → specific, arc42/C4), headings without numbers, heavy sections folded under ``, the Overview section carrying its diagram per the Diagram Plan. Restructuring reorders and clarifies what the source ALREADY says — per the Mission's out-of-scope line, migration only transforms what already exists: do not author a new section (Golden DX, FR, or any other) the source spec never had; a section the target structure calls for but the source lacks stays absent, marked for `evolve`/`sdd-continue` to fill later, never silently invented here. The `SCOPE_TYPE` anchor is the one exception, not a violation of it: structural v2 metadata, not content — write it (or correct it) with the value the operator confirmed in STEP_4, for every scope spec that lacks it; a scope spec without `SCOPE_TYPE` cannot be gated by `REQUIRED_SECTIONS` at all, so leaving it unwritten would silently exempt the migrated spec from the very check the restructure is supposed to make possible. Collapse converged decisions via `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/compression.directive.xml")` (superseded marked per `AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION`, never silently dropped; merges propagated to code references) — a Decision Log entry's TEXT is changed only through supersession, never edited in place. Rewrite operator-facing text to flat engineering Russian in the same pass, per `AX_MIGRATION_COMPREHENSION_PASS` — decode every empty label and code-only term from the actual code, replace every metaphor with the literal mechanism, never guess (code / IDs / status tokens / BDD keywords / paths stay English). Gate per scope: integrityCheck ToolCall below — strict v2 structure, folds, real mermaid parse, and the language lint (`SDD_LANGUAGE_CALQUE`) that gates the comprehension pass above mechanically — clean. Set the unit `**Status:** DONE`. npx gennady sdd-check --all specs/ Inputs : =exact current migration unit scope just restructured in this STEP_7. Use integrityCheck.

Step.Goal: Prove the migration is complete; retire the working layer.
Step.Action: Final gate, all green or `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL`: migrationState ToolCall below → `FLOW_VERSION=v2` · integrityCheck ToolCall below clean (every migrated scope spec now carries `SCOPE_TYPE` from STEP_7, so this run exercises the strict `REQUIRED_SECTIONS` gate for real, not the dormant no-`SCOPE_TYPE` path) · zero original Task-IDs and zero `*.task-*.md` names remain (migrationIds ToolCall below DRY-RUN reports nothing to do) · every unit `**Status:** DONE` · per migrated module, run inventoryCheck ToolCall below — the inventory-reverse verdict (spec Entity Inventory vs. code's real exports) and any finding introduced BY the migration's own rewrite must be clean, or `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL`. A finding that can only be closed by authoring new content (missing DbC contract, missing header — legacy the Mission's `Out of scope` line forbids inventing text for here) is judged mechanically against baseline, never by eye: reproduces on the pre-migration state (`git stash` this run's diff, re-run the same lint command, `git stash pop`) → pre-existing, does NOT block this gate — list it to the operator as post-migration backlog, pointed at `reconcile`/`recover` for a separate pass. Does not reproduce on baseline → the migration itself introduced it → `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL`, same as any other red finding here. With the operator's confirmation remove the `migration/` layer (its content is now embodied in the repo; git history keeps the record). Return control to the caller — script readiness is the router's separate gate. Return exact post-mutation alias `migrationState`; the caller reuses it as its active routing snapshot and must not refresh again. npx gennady sdd-state Use migrationState. npx gennady sdd-check --all . Use integrityCheck. npx gennady sdd-migrate ids --from-plan Use migrationIds. npx gennady lint --spec= --inventory-reverse Inputs , : /=each exact migrated module spec and its code root recorded by the unit. Use inventoryCheck.

SddMigrationV1V2.ReferenceData:
**What changes:** `tasks///.task-NN.md` → co-located `specs///.task.-.md` + `*.3-tasks.md` indexes · `TSK-NN` (or `-NNN`) → `-` · tickets gain `` anchors · spec sections restructured to the v2 order (Overview + diagram, no heading numbers, heavy detail folded) · operator-facing text → flat Russian · redundant decisions collapsed.
**What is NOT touched:** existing legacy `D-N` entries stay byte-for-byte as append-only history; every NEW decision uses `-DL-N`. `FR-NN` / `NFC-NN` and scope-prefixed requirement/scenario IDs stay (optional later reformat to BDD `-REQ-N`) · `UTF-8` / `UTF-16` and similar are NOT IDs — never replaced.
**Tooling state — all four mechanical modes are real tools:** `sdd-migrate plan` (generate / `--verify` the migration layer — the Section Map arrives pre-filled by `mapHeadingToSection`; the Ticket Map's New-ID arrives pre-filled tolerantly from each ticket's v1 Meta where it already carries ACR/slug-shaped fields — a best-effort seed the agent still reviews, never authoritative; `--verify` fails on any leftover `UNMAPPED` target or a New ID that fails `NEW_ID_REGEX`, which requires `` UPPERCASE) · `sdd-migrate anchors` (section markers) · `sdd-migrate ids` (word-boundary ID replacement, `--from-plan`, self-gating on zero leftovers) · `sdd-migrate move` (per-scope relocation to the Ticket Map's destination — module co-location when the unit has a module, a flat scope-level destination legal for a scope without modules — + index scaffolding + relative markdown-link rewriting inside every moved ticket and every referencing file in the same zones + automatic removal of the now-emptied `tasks//`). What stays semantic — closing `UNMAPPED` rows and correcting the Ticket Map pre-fill (STEP_3) and the restructure/compression/comprehension pass (STEP_7) — is agent work executed against a verified plan and gated by strict per-scope `sdd-check` plus, at the final gate, `gennady lint --inventory-reverse` per migrated module (STEP_8).
**Mixed state is first-class:** `sdd-check` detects the flow version per scope. On a v1 repo a scope counts as migrated (v2, strict) only positively: `tasks//` removed AND the co-located `.3-tasks.md` present — both produced by `sdd-migrate move`. A scope that merely never had tasks stays lenient until the repo flips. Migration therefore runs one scope at a time — each migrated scope is checked strictly immediately, no waiting for the whole repo.
**Parallel dispatch:** unit files are self-sufficient — STEP_3 and STEP_7 fan out one unit per agent (units never share files); the repo-wide mechanical steps (anchors / ids / move) run centrally between the fan-outs, per `migration/README.md`'s G1–G8 order.
SddMigrationV1V2.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (`AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `🔁 MIG_R · v1→v2 · step= · tickets= · ready=`. Breadcrumb milestones for this flow (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): Inventory · Plan · Anchors · Ack · IDs · Move · Restructure · Verify.
One line, its own paragraph below the service line — a blank line separates the two (per `MESSAGE_LAYOUT`); a single `\n` with no blank line is a contract defect, markdown renders it fused onto the service line as one run-on. This session's milestones, each rendered ` `, with a status marker chosen for legibility on BOTH light and dark themes — no half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓`) anywhere, they vanish depending on theme. Status set: `✅` done · `👷` active (the step running now) · `◻️` not yet reached. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
